body.text: Cómo medir el ahorro

Siga cuatro cifras por trabajo: pliegos hasta el primer pliego correcto, DeltaE en ese pliego, tiempo de puesta a punto, y tinta y papel consumidos antes de la aprobación. Mejorar las dos primeras casi siempre arrastra las otras dos hacia abajo.
Por dónde empezar

La mayoría de los impresores ya posee un dispositivo de medición. Las ganancias más rápidas suelen venir de combinar el preajuste CIP3/CIP4 con el control closed-loop: la prensa arranca cerca del objetivo y luego lo alcanza en menos pasadas. Una validación de consola gratuita confirma si su pupitre es apto.

title: ISO 12647-2, explained
excerpt: A plain-language guide to ISO 12647-2 for offset: what it standardizes (substrates, primaries, tone value increase, tolerances) and why it makes color repeatable.
lead: ISO 12647-2 is the reference that turns good color from an opinion into a target. Here is what it actually specifies for sheetfed and web offset, without the jargon.
paragraphs: ISO 12647-2 is the international process standard for offset printing. It defines the aim values a job should hit so that the same file prints consistently, whether it runs today or next month, on one press or another.
It starts with substrate classes. Different paper categories (for example gloss coated, matte coated, uncoated) have their own aim values, because the same ink looks different on different stock.
It defines the primaries: the target Lab values for solid cyan, magenta, yellow and black, plus the two-color overprints. These are the anchor colors your process is judged against.
It defines tone value increase, often called dot gain: how much the midtones grow on press, expressed as curves. Controlling TVI is what keeps images from going muddy or flat.

Finally it sets tolerances: how far a production sheet may deviate from aim, and how much it may vary across the run. Conformance is judged from measurements taken under defined conditions (M0 or M1), which is why the measurement condition matters as much as the number.

On the floor, a defined target is what makes color repeatable. The operator and a closed-loop system chase the same aim values, makeready is faster, and brand owners get consistent results they can trust.

ISO 12647 is not alone. G7 and GRACoL approach the same goal through gray balance, and Fogra characterization data underpins many profiles. They are complementary ways to reach a known, measurable target.

Reaching the standard takes three things: measurement, a defined target, and ideally closed-loop control to hold it during the run. A free console validation tells you whether your press is equipped to get there.

body.text: ISO 12647-2 is the reference that turns good color from an opinion into a target. It is what lets a job printed today match the same job printed next month, or in another plant. Here is what it actually specifies for sheetfed and web offset, without the jargon.
What ISO 12647-2 standardizes

items: Substrate classes, with defined paper white and gloss.
Aim values for the process primaries (cyan, magenta, yellow, black) in CIELAB.
Tone value increase (TVI) curves, by screening and substrate.
Gray balance, so neutrals stay neutral across the tonal range.
Tolerances: how far a production sheet may deviate and still conform.

body.text: Why it makes color repeatable

By fixing the targets and the acceptable spread around them, ISO 12647-2 removes the guesswork. Two operators, two shifts or two sites print to the same numbers instead of to personal judgement, which is what makes the result repeatable.
Substrates and ink primaries

Color is always relative to the paper it sits on, so the standard defines substrate classes and the Lab values the primaries should hit on each. Match your paper to the right class first; the rest of the aim values follow from there.
Tone value increase and tolerances

Ink spreads as it transfers and dries, so a 50% dot prints darker than 50%. ISO 12647-2 specifies how much TVI is expected and the tolerance around it. Holding TVI and gray balance is usually what separates a conforming sheet from a near miss.
Printing to ISO 12647-2 in practice

Standardize the substrate and inks, characterize the press, then control each run against the aim values with a color bar and a measurement device. Closed-loop control keeps you inside tolerance from the first sheet to the last, not only at spot checks.

de.title: ISO 12647-2, erklärt
de.excerpt: Ein verständlicher Leitfaden zur ISO 12647-2 für den Offsetdruck: was sie standardisiert (Bedruckstoffe, Primärfarben, Tonwertzuwachs, Toleranzen) und warum sie Farbe wiederholbar macht.
de.lead: Die ISO 12647-2 ist die Referenz, die gute Farbe aus einer Meinung zu einem Zielwert macht. So funktioniert sie für Bogen- und Rollenoffset, ohne Fachjargon.

body.text: Die ISO 12647-2 ist die Referenz, die gute Farbe aus einer Meinung zu einem Zielwert macht. Sie sorgt dafür, dass ein heute gedruckter Auftrag mit demselben Auftrag im nächsten Monat oder in einem anderen Werk übereinstimmt. Hier ist, was sie für Bogen- und Rollenoffset tatsächlich festlegt, ohne Fachjargon.
Was die ISO 12647-2 standardisiert

items: Bedruckstoffklassen, mit definiertem Papierweiß und Glanz.
Sollwerte für die Prozess-Primärfarben (Cyan, Magenta, Gelb, Schwarz) in CIELAB.
Tonwertzuwachs-Kurven (TVI), nach Rasterung und Bedruckstoff.
Graubalance, damit Neutraltöne über den gesamten Tonwertbereich neutral bleiben.
Toleranzen: wie weit ein Produktionsbogen abweichen darf und dennoch konform ist.

body.text: Warum sie Farbe wiederholbar macht

Indem sie die Zielwerte und die zulässige Streuung darum festlegt, nimmt die ISO 12647-2 das Rätselraten heraus. Zwei Bediener, zwei Schichten oder zwei Standorte drucken auf dieselben Zahlen statt auf das persönliche Urteil, und genau das macht das Ergebnis wiederholbar.
Bedruckstoffe und Druckfarben-Primärfarben

Farbe ist immer relativ zum Papier, auf dem sie sitzt. Daher definiert der Standard Bedruckstoffklassen und die Lab-Werte, die die Primärfarben auf jeder erreichen sollen. Ordnen Sie Ihr Papier zuerst der richtigen Klasse zu; die übrigen Sollwerte folgen daraus.
Tonwertzuwachs und Toleranzen

Farbe breitet sich beim Übertragen und Trocknen aus, sodass ein 50%-Punkt dunkler als 50% druckt. Die ISO 12647-2 legt fest, wie viel Tonwertzuwachs erwartet wird und welche Toleranz darum gilt. TVI und Graubalance zu halten ist meist das, was einen konformen Bogen von einem knappen Fehlschlag unterscheidet.
ISO 12647-2 in der Praxis drucken

Standardisieren Sie Bedruckstoff und Farben, charakterisieren Sie die Druckmaschine und regeln Sie dann jede Auflage mit einem Farbmessstreifen und einem Messgerät gegen die Sollwerte. Die Closed-Loop-Regelung hält Sie vom ersten bis zum letzten Bogen in der Toleranz, nicht nur bei Stichproben.

fr.title: ISO 12647-2, expliquée
fr.excerpt: Un guide en langage clair de l'ISO 12647-2 pour l'offset : ce qu'elle standardise (substrats, primaires, engraissement, tolérances) et pourquoi elle rend la couleur répétable.
fr.lead: L'ISO 12647-2 est la référence qui transforme une bonne couleur d'une opinion en une cible. Voici ce qu'elle spécifie réellement pour l'offset feuille et rotative, sans jargon.

body.text: L'ISO 12647-2 est la référence qui transforme une bonne couleur d'une opinion en une cible. C'est elle qui permet à un travail imprimé aujourd'hui de correspondre au même travail imprimé le mois prochain, ou dans un autre site. Voici ce qu'elle spécifie réellement pour l'offset feuille et rotative, sans jargon.
Ce que standardise l'ISO 12647-2

items: Des classes de substrat, avec un blanc papier et un brillant définis.
Des valeurs cibles pour les primaires du procédé (cyan, magenta, jaune, noir) en CIELAB.
Des courbes d'engraissement (TVI), selon la trame et le substrat.
L'équilibre des gris, pour que les neutres restent neutres sur toute la plage tonale.
Des tolérances : de combien une feuille de production peut s'écarter tout en restant conforme.

body.text: Pourquoi elle rend la couleur répétable

En fixant les cibles et l'écart acceptable autour, l'ISO 12647-2 retire le pifomètre. Deux opérateurs, deux équipes ou deux sites impriment sur les mêmes chiffres plutôt que sur un jugement personnel, et c'est ce qui rend le résultat répétable.
Substrats et primaires d'encre

La couleur est toujours relative au papier sur lequel elle repose ; la norme définit donc des classes de substrat et les valeurs Lab que les primaires doivent atteindre sur chacune. Rattachez d'abord votre papier à la bonne classe ; le reste des valeurs cibles en découle.
Engraissement et tolérances

L'encre s'étale en se transférant et en séchant, si bien qu'un point de 50 % imprime plus foncé que 50 %. L'ISO 12647-2 précise l'engraissement attendu et la tolérance autour. Tenir l'engraissement et l'équilibre des gris est généralement ce qui sépare une feuille conforme d'un quasi-échec.
Imprimer selon l'ISO 12647-2 en pratique

Standardisez le substrat et les encres, caractérisez la presse, puis pilotez chaque tirage contre les valeurs cibles avec une barre de contrôle couleur et un dispositif de mesure. Le contrôle closed-loop vous maintient dans la tolérance de la première à la dernière feuille, pas seulement aux contrôles ponctuels.

it.title: ISO 12647-2, spiegata
it.excerpt: Una guida in linguaggio semplice alla ISO 12647-2 per l'offset: cosa standardizza (supporti, primari, incremento del valore tonale, tolleranze) e perché rende il colore ripetibile.
it.lead: La ISO 12647-2 è il riferimento che trasforma un buon colore da opinione a target. Ecco cosa specifica davvero per l'offset a foglio e a bobina, senza gergo.

body.text: La ISO 12647-2 è il riferimento che trasforma un buon colore da opinione a target. È ciò che permette a un lavoro stampato oggi di coincidere con lo stesso lavoro stampato il mese prossimo, o in un altro stabilimento. Ecco cosa specifica davvero per l'offset a foglio e a bobina, senza gergo.
Cosa standardizza la ISO 12647-2

items: Classi di supporto, con bianco carta e brillantezza definiti.
Valori target per i primari di processo (cyan, magenta, giallo, nero) in CIELAB.
Curve di incremento del valore tonale (TVI), per retinatura e supporto.
Bilanciamento del grigio, perché i neutri restino neutri su tutta la gamma tonale.
Tolleranze: di quanto un foglio di produzione può scostarsi restando conforme.

body.text: Perché rende il colore ripetibile

Fissando i target e la dispersione accettabile attorno, la ISO 12647-2 elimina le supposizioni. Due operatori, due turni o due stabilimenti stampano sugli stessi numeri anziché sul giudizio personale, ed è questo a rendere ripetibile il risultato.
Supporti e primari di inchiostro

Il colore è sempre relativo alla carta su cui poggia, perciò la norma definisce classi di supporto e i valori Lab che i primari devono raggiungere su ciascuna. Si abbini prima la carta alla classe giusta; il resto dei valori target ne deriva.
Incremento del valore tonale e tolleranze

L'inchiostro si allarga trasferendosi e asciugando, così un punto del 50% stampa più scuro del 50%. La ISO 12647-2 specifica quanto incremento è atteso e la tolleranza attorno. Tenere il TVI e il bilanciamento del grigio è di solito ciò che separa un foglio conforme da un quasi-errore.
Stampare secondo la ISO 12647-2 in pratica

Standardizzare supporto e inchiostri, caratterizzare la macchina, quindi controllare ogni tiratura rispetto ai valori target con una barra colore e un dispositivo di misura. Il controllo closed-loop mantiene in tolleranza dal primo all'ultimo foglio, non solo a campione.

es.title: ISO 12647-2, explicada
es.excerpt: Una guía en lenguaje claro de la ISO 12647-2 para offset: qué estandariza (sustratos, primarios, ganancia de punto, tolerancias) y por qué hace el color repetible.
es.lead: La ISO 12647-2 es la referencia que convierte un buen color de una opinión en un objetivo. Esto es lo que especifica realmente para offset de pliego y de bobina, sin jerga.

body.text: La ISO 12647-2 es la referencia que convierte un buen color de una opinión en un objetivo. Es lo que permite que un trabajo impreso hoy coincida con el mismo trabajo impreso el mes que viene, o en otra planta. Esto es lo que especifica realmente para offset de pliego y de bobina, sin jerga.
Qué estandariza la ISO 12647-2

items: Clases de sustrato, con blanco de papel y brillo definidos.
Valores objetivo para los primarios de proceso (cian, magenta, amarillo, negro) en CIELAB.
Curvas de ganancia de punto (TVI), por trama y sustrato.
Equilibrio de grises, para que los neutros se mantengan neutros en todo el rango tonal.
Tolerancias: cuánto puede desviarse un pliego de producción y seguir siendo conforme.

body.text: Por qué hace el color repetible

Al fijar los objetivos y la dispersión aceptable a su alrededor, la ISO 12647-2 elimina las conjeturas. Dos operadores, dos turnos o dos plantas imprimen a las mismas cifras en lugar de al juicio personal, y eso es lo que hace repetible el resultado.
Sustratos y primarios de tinta

El color siempre es relativo al papel sobre el que se asienta, así que la norma define clases de sustrato y los valores Lab que los primarios deben alcanzar en cada una. Asigne primero su papel a la clase correcta; el resto de los valores objetivo se deriva de ahí.
Ganancia de punto y tolerancias

La tinta se extiende al transferirse y secarse, de modo que un punto del 50% imprime más oscuro que el 50%. La ISO 12647-2 especifica cuánta ganancia se espera y la tolerancia a su alrededor. Mantener la ganancia y el equilibrio de grises suele ser lo que separa un pliego conforme de un casi fallo.
Imprimir según la ISO 12647-2 en la práctica

Estandarice el sustrato y las tintas, caracterice la prensa y luego controle cada tirada contra los valores objetivo con una barra de color y un dispositivo de medición. El control closed-loop le mantiene en tolerancia del primer al último pliego, no solo en controles puntuales.

title: DeltaE: what tolerance is acceptable?
excerpt: What DeltaE and DeltaE00 mean in printing, what tolerances are realistic for process and brand colors, and how to hold them in production.
lead: DeltaE is how the print industry puts a number on color difference. But the right answer to what DeltaE is acceptable depends on what you are measuring. Here is a practical guide.
paragraphs: DeltaE is a single number for the distance between two colors in Lab space. A measured sheet and its target each have a Lab value, and DeltaE is how far apart they are. The smaller the number, the closer the match.

There are several formulas. The older DeltaE76 is a simple geometric distance; modern standards use DeltaE00 (CIE2000), which weights the calculation to match how the human eye actually perceives differences, especially in neutrals and saturated colors.

As a rough guide, a DeltaE00 around 1 is barely perceptible to a trained eye, a few units is noticeable on a critical color, and larger values are obvious. These are guidelines, not hard rules, because perceptibility depends on the color and the viewing conditions.

Realistic tolerances depend on the color. Process primaries are usually held to the limits set by ISO 12647 or G7. Brand and spot colors are stricter, because a customer recognizes their signature color instantly; brand owners often ask for DeltaE00 of 2 or less on those.
Color drifts in production for physical reasons: substrate batch, ink, fountain solution, temperature and plate wear all move the result during a run.

Holding DeltaE means three things: measure under the correct condition (M0 or M1), set a clear target, and correct continuously. Closed-loop control corrects every few sheets rather than at occasional checks, which is what keeps DeltaE inside tolerance from first sheet to last.

The payoff is direct: tighter DeltaE means fewer rejects, less makeready and rerun waste, and brand colors that look the same every time. A free console validation confirms whether your press can run that kind of control.

body.text: DeltaE is how the print industry puts a single number on the difference between two colors. But the right answer to what DeltaE is acceptable depends entirely on what you are measuring and who is judging it. Here is a practical guide.
What DeltaE measures

DeltaE is the distance between two colors in a color space. The larger the number, the more visible the difference. As a rough anchor, a DeltaE around 1 is barely perceptible to a trained eye, while larger values become obvious side by side.
DeltaE76 versus DeltaE2000

DeltaE76 is the original, simple Euclidean distance, but it does not match human perception evenly across the spectrum. DeltaE2000 (dE00) corrects for that and is the modern default for print tolerances. Always state which formula a tolerance refers to.
What tolerance is realistic

items: Process colors to ISO 12647: primaries within a few dE00, tightening as you approach the target.
Brand and spot colors: brand owners often ask for dE00 of 2 or tighter on critical colors.
Substrate matters: an uncoated or low-quality stock makes very tight tolerances physically harder to hold.

body.text: How to hold tolerance in production

Pick the formula and target, print a color bar on every sheet, and measure continuously rather than spot-checking. Closed-loop control corrects ink zones automatically as the run drifts, which is what keeps DeltaE inside tolerance from start to finish.

de.title: DeltaE: welche Toleranz ist akzeptabel?
de.excerpt: Was DeltaE und DeltaE00 im Druck bedeuten, welche Toleranzen für Prozess- und Markenfarben realistisch sind und wie Sie sie in der Produktion halten.
de.lead: DeltaE ist die Art, wie die Druckbranche dem Farbunterschied eine Zahl gibt. Aber die richtige Antwort auf die Frage, welches DeltaE akzeptabel ist, hängt davon ab, was Sie messen. Hier ein praxisnaher Leitfaden.

body.text: DeltaE ist die Art, wie die Druckbranche dem Unterschied zwischen zwei Farben eine einzige Zahl gibt. Aber die richtige Antwort darauf, welches DeltaE akzeptabel ist, hängt vollständig davon ab, was Sie messen und wer es beurteilt. Hier ein praxisnaher Leitfaden.
Was DeltaE misst

DeltaE ist der Abstand zwischen zwei Farben in einem Farbraum. Je größer die Zahl, desto sichtbarer der Unterschied. Als grobe Orientierung: Ein DeltaE um 1 ist für ein geschultes Auge kaum wahrnehmbar, während größere Werte im direkten Vergleich offensichtlich werden.
DeltaE76 gegenüber DeltaE2000

DeltaE76 ist der ursprüngliche, einfache euklidische Abstand, der die menschliche Wahrnehmung jedoch nicht gleichmäßig über das Spektrum abbildet. DeltaE2000 (dE00) korrigiert das und ist der moderne Standard für Drucktoleranzen. Geben Sie immer an, auf welche Formel sich eine Toleranz bezieht.
Welche Toleranz realistisch ist

items: Prozessfarben nach ISO 12647: Primärfarben innerhalb weniger dE00, enger werdend, je näher Sie am Zielwert sind.
Marken- und Sonderfarben: Markeninhaber verlangen für kritische Farben oft dE00 von 2 oder enger.
Der Bedruckstoff zählt: ein ungestrichenes oder minderwertiges Papier macht sehr enge Toleranzen physikalisch schwerer haltbar.

body.text: Wie Sie die Toleranz in der Produktion halten

Legen Sie Formel und Zielwert fest, drucken Sie einen Farbmessstreifen auf jedem Bogen und messen Sie kontinuierlich statt stichprobenartig. Die Closed-Loop-Regelung korrigiert die Farbzonen automatisch, wenn die Auflage driftet, und genau das hält DeltaE von Anfang bis Ende in der Toleranz.

fr.title: DeltaE : quelle tolérance est acceptable ?
fr.excerpt: Ce que signifient DeltaE et DeltaE00 en impression, quelles tolérances sont réalistes pour les couleurs de procédé et de marque, et comment les tenir en production.
fr.lead: Le DeltaE, c'est la façon dont l'industrie de l'impression met un chiffre sur l'écart de couleur. Mais la bonne réponse à « quel DeltaE est acceptable » dépend de ce que vous mesurez. Voici un guide pratique.

body.text: Le DeltaE, c'est la façon dont l'industrie de l'impression met un seul chiffre sur l'écart entre deux couleurs. Mais la bonne réponse à « quel DeltaE est acceptable » dépend entièrement de ce que vous mesurez et de qui le juge. Voici un guide pratique.
Ce que mesure le DeltaE

Le DeltaE est la distance entre deux couleurs dans un espace colorimétrique. Plus le chiffre est élevé, plus l'écart est visible. Pour situer : un DeltaE autour de 1 est à peine perceptible pour un œil exercé, tandis que des valeurs plus élevées deviennent évidentes côte à côte.
DeltaE76 face à DeltaE2000

Le DeltaE76 est la distance euclidienne d'origine, simple, mais qui ne colle pas uniformément à la perception humaine sur tout le spectre. Le DeltaE2000 (dE00) corrige cela et constitue le standard moderne pour les tolérances d'impression. Précisez toujours à quelle formule une tolérance se rapporte.
Quelle tolérance est réaliste

items: Couleurs de procédé selon l'ISO 12647 : primaires à quelques dE00, de plus en plus serrées à mesure que vous approchez de la cible.
Couleurs de marque et tons directs : les marques demandent souvent un dE00 de 2 ou moins sur les couleurs critiques.
Le substrat compte : un papier non couché ou de faible qualité rend les tolérances très serrées physiquement plus difficiles à tenir.

body.text: Comment tenir la tolérance en production

Choisissez la formule et la cible, imprimez une barre de contrôle couleur sur chaque feuille, et mesurez en continu plutôt que par sondage. Le contrôle closed-loop corrige les zones d'encrage automatiquement à mesure que le tirage dérive, et c'est ce qui maintient le DeltaE dans la tolérance du début à la fin.

it.title: DeltaE: quale tolleranza è accettabile?
it.excerpt: Cosa significano DeltaE e DeltaE00 in stampa, quali tolleranze sono realistiche per colori di processo e di marca, e come tenerle in produzione.
it.lead: Il DeltaE è il modo in cui il settore della stampa mette un numero sulla differenza di colore. Ma la risposta giusta a quale DeltaE sia accettabile dipende da cosa si misura. Ecco una guida pratica.

body.text: Il DeltaE è il modo in cui il settore della stampa mette un singolo numero sulla differenza tra due colori. Ma la risposta giusta a quale DeltaE sia accettabile dipende interamente da cosa si misura e da chi giudica. Ecco una guida pratica.
Cosa misura il DeltaE

Il DeltaE è la distanza tra due colori in uno spazio colore. Più grande è il numero, più visibile è la differenza. Come riferimento di massima, un DeltaE intorno a 1 è appena percettibile per un occhio allenato, mentre valori maggiori diventano evidenti se accostati.
DeltaE76 rispetto a DeltaE2000

Il DeltaE76 è la distanza euclidea originale, semplice, ma non aderisce uniformemente alla percezione umana su tutto lo spettro. Il DeltaE2000 (dE00) corregge questo ed è lo standard moderno per le tolleranze di stampa. Indicare sempre a quale formula si riferisce una tolleranza.
Quale tolleranza è realistica

items: Colori di processo secondo ISO 12647: primari entro pochi dE00, sempre più stretti man mano che ci si avvicina al target.
Colori di marca e tinte piatte: i brand chiedono spesso un dE00 di 2 o inferiore sui colori critici.
Il supporto conta: una carta non patinata o di bassa qualità rende fisicamente più difficile tenere tolleranze molto strette.

body.text: Come tenere la tolleranza in produzione

Scegliere la formula e il target, stampare una barra colore su ogni foglio e misurare in continuo anziché a campione. Il controllo closed-loop corregge automaticamente le zone di inchiostro mentre la tiratura deriva, ed è questo a tenere il DeltaE in tolleranza dall'inizio alla fine.

es.title: DeltaE: ¿qué tolerancia es aceptable?
es.excerpt: Qué significan DeltaE y DeltaE00 en impresión, qué tolerancias son realistas para colores de proceso y de marca, y cómo mantenerlas en producción.
es.lead: El DeltaE es la forma en que el sector de la impresión pone un número a la diferencia de color. Pero la respuesta correcta a qué DeltaE es aceptable depende de lo que esté midiendo. Aquí tiene una guía práctica.

body.text: El DeltaE es la forma en que el sector de la impresión pone un único número a la diferencia entre dos colores. Pero la respuesta correcta a qué DeltaE es aceptable depende por completo de lo que esté midiendo y de quién lo juzgue. Aquí tiene una guía práctica.
Qué mide el DeltaE

El DeltaE es la distancia entre dos colores en un espacio de color. Cuanto mayor es el número, más visible es la diferencia. Como referencia aproximada, un DeltaE en torno a 1 es apenas perceptible para un ojo entrenado, mientras que valores mayores se vuelven evidentes uno al lado del otro.
DeltaE76 frente a DeltaE2000

El DeltaE76 es la distancia euclidiana original, sencilla, pero no se ajusta de manera uniforme a la percepción humana en todo el espectro. El DeltaE2000 (dE00) corrige eso y es el estándar moderno para tolerancias de impresión. Indique siempre a qué fórmula se refiere una tolerancia.
Qué tolerancia es realista

items: Colores de proceso según ISO 12647: primarios dentro de unos pocos dE00, más ajustados a medida que se acerca al objetivo.
Colores de marca y tintas directas: las marcas suelen pedir un dE00 de 2 o menos en los colores críticos.
El sustrato importa: un papel no estucado o de baja calidad hace físicamente más difícil mantener tolerancias muy estrechas.

body.text: Cómo mantener la tolerancia en producción

Elija la fórmula y el objetivo, imprima una barra de color en cada pliego y mida de forma continua en lugar de por muestreo. El control closed-loop corrige las zonas de tinta automáticamente a medida que la tirada deriva, y eso es lo que mantiene el DeltaE en tolerancia de principio a fin.

title: PPWR & DPP: printer checklist
excerpt: What the EU PPWR and Digital Product Passport mean for packaging printers, and a practical checklist to get color, data and traceability ready.
lead: The EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) and the Digital Product Passport (DPP) are reshaping packaging. Here is a printer-focused checklist of what to prepare.
paragraphs: Two EU initiatives are changing packaging at the same time. PPWR pushes recyclability, recycled content and waste reduction across packaging. The Digital Product Passport adds traceable, shareable data about a product and how it was made. Both reach back to the printer.

Material and recyclability come first. Substrate and ink choices, and design-for-recycling decisions, increasingly determine whether a pack is compliant. Printers are part of that conversation with brand owners and converters.
Waste reduction is now also a sustainability metric, not only a cost. Every sheet wasted at makeready is material wasted, so production efficiency and compliance now point in the same direction.

Data and traceability are the new requirement. A DPP means information about the product and process must be captured and made available. Color and quality data, such as validation records and DeltaE measurements per job, become assets rather than paperwork.
This is where color control connects to compliance. A closed-loop system produces auditable color data for every run, which supports brand-owner reporting and the traceability that DPP expects.

A practical checklist: standardize to ISO 12647 or G7; capture measurement and validation records per job; cut makeready waste; document materials and inks; and make your data exportable so it can feed a passport.
Rutherford sits on the color and data side of this shift: closed-loop color with traceable records. A free console validation is a low-effort first step to see where your press stands.

sources.label: EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation

body.text: The EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) and the Digital Product Passport (DPP) are reshaping how packaging is designed, produced and tracked. For printers and converters, that means new demands on data, traceability and color. Here is a printer-focused checklist of what to prepare.
What PPWR changes

PPWR pushes packaging toward recyclability, recycled content and waste reduction across the EU. It affects substrate and ink choices, design for recycling, and the documentation you need to show compliance, which in turn affects how you set up and prove a job.
What the Digital Product Passport adds

The DPP attaches a digital record to a product, accessible through a data carrier such as a code on the pack. For printers, the relevant part is producing and tracking the data and the printed carrier reliably, job after job.
Printer readiness checklist

items: Standardize color to ISO 12647 so jobs are repeatable and documented.
Capture color data per job: targets, measurements and DeltaE results.
Make that data traceable and exportable, not locked in an operator's head.
Validate that codes and carriers print and scan reliably on your substrates.
Review substrates and inks for recyclability and recycled-content requirements.
Keep an auditable record linking each run to its standard and its results.

body.text: Where color and data meet

Compliance is easier when color control already produces clean, auditable data. A closed-loop workflow records what was printed and how close it was to target, which is exactly the kind of traceable evidence PPWR and DPP reward.

To put this into practice, Rutherford built [PPWRConnect.com](https://ppwrconnect.com), a platform that helps packaging printers and converters get PPWR and DPP ready: it brings recyclability, recycled-content and color-traceability data together so compliance can be documented job by job and connected to the Digital Product Passport.

de.lead: Die EU-Verpackungsverordnung (PPWR) und der Digitale Produktpass (DPP) gestalten Verpackung neu. Hier ist eine auf Druckereien zugeschnittene Checkliste, was vorzubereiten ist.

body.text: Die EU-Verpackungs- und Verpackungsabfallverordnung (PPWR) und der Digitale Produktpass (DPP) verändern, wie Verpackung gestaltet, produziert und nachverfolgt wird. Für Druckereien und Verarbeiter bedeutet das neue Anforderungen an Daten, Rückverfolgbarkeit und Farbe. Hier ist eine auf Druckereien zugeschnittene Checkliste, was vorzubereiten ist.
Was die PPWR ändert

Die PPWR treibt Verpackung EU-weit in Richtung Recyclingfähigkeit, Recyclinganteil und Abfallreduzierung. Sie betrifft die Wahl von Bedruckstoff und Farben, das Design for Recycling und die Dokumentation, die Sie zum Konformitätsnachweis benötigen, was wiederum beeinflusst, wie Sie einen Auftrag einrichten und nachweisen.
Was der Digitale Produktpass hinzufügt

Der DPP hängt einen digitalen Datensatz an ein Produkt, zugänglich über einen Datenträger wie einen Code auf der Verpackung. Für Druckereien ist der relevante Teil, die Daten und den gedruckten Datenträger zuverlässig zu erzeugen und nachzuverfolgen, Auftrag für Auftrag.
Checkliste für die Bereitschaft der Druckerei

items: Farbe auf die ISO 12647 standardisieren, damit Aufträge wiederholbar und dokumentiert sind.
Farbdaten pro Auftrag erfassen: Zielwerte, Messungen und DeltaE-Ergebnisse.
Diese Daten rückverfolgbar und exportierbar machen, nicht im Kopf eines Bedieners eingeschlossen.
Prüfen, dass Codes und Datenträger auf Ihren Bedruckstoffen zuverlässig drucken und scannen.
Bedruckstoffe und Farben auf Recyclingfähigkeit und Anforderungen an den Recyclinganteil prüfen.
Einen prüffähigen Nachweis führen, der jede Auflage mit ihrem Standard und ihren Ergebnissen verknüpft.

body.text: Wo Farbe und Daten zusammenkommen

Compliance ist einfacher, wenn die Farbregelung bereits saubere, prüffähige Daten erzeugt. Ein Closed-Loop-Workflow protokolliert, was gedruckt wurde und wie nah es am Zielwert war, genau die Art rückverfolgbarer Nachweise, die PPWR und DPP belohnen.

fr.lead: Le règlement européen sur les emballages (PPWR) et le passeport produit numérique (DPP) redessinent l'emballage. Voici une checklist orientée imprimeur de ce qu'il faut préparer.

body.text: Le règlement européen sur les emballages et les déchets d'emballages (PPWR) et le passeport produit numérique (DPP) transforment la façon dont l'emballage est conçu, produit et suivi. Pour les imprimeurs et transformateurs, cela signifie de nouvelles exigences en matière de données, de traçabilité et de couleur. Voici une checklist orientée imprimeur de ce qu'il faut préparer.
Ce que change la PPWR

La PPWR pousse l'emballage vers la recyclabilité, le contenu recyclé et la réduction des déchets dans toute l'UE. Elle influe sur le choix des substrats et des encres, l'éco-conception et la documentation nécessaire pour prouver la conformité, ce qui à son tour influe sur la façon dont vous calez et prouvez un travail.
Ce qu'ajoute le passeport produit numérique

Le DPP attache un enregistrement numérique à un produit, accessible via un porteur de données comme un code sur l'emballage. Pour les imprimeurs, la partie pertinente est de produire et de suivre les données et le porteur imprimé de façon fiable, travail après travail.
Checklist de préparation de l'imprimeur

items: Standardiser la couleur sur l'ISO 12647 pour que les travaux soient répétables et documentés.
Capturer les données couleur par travail : cibles, mesures et résultats DeltaE.
Rendre ces données traçables et exportables, pas enfermées dans la tête d'un opérateur.
Vérifier que les codes et porteurs s'impriment et se scannent de façon fiable sur vos substrats.
Examiner substrats et encres au regard de la recyclabilité et des exigences de contenu recyclé.
Tenir un enregistrement auditable reliant chaque tirage à son standard et à ses résultats.

body.text: Là où couleur et données se rejoignent

La conformité est plus simple quand le contrôle couleur produit déjà des données propres et auditables. Un workflow closed-loop enregistre ce qui a été imprimé et à quel point c'était proche de la cible, exactement le type de preuve traçable que la PPWR et le DPP récompensent.

title: CIP3/CIP4 ink presetting
excerpt: What CIP3/CIP4 (PPF, JDF) ink presetting is, how it opens ink keys from prepress data, and how it pairs with closed-loop color to shorten makeready.
lead: CIP3/CIP4 presetting is one of the cheapest ways to shorten makeready: it opens your ink keys from prepress data instead of from zero. Here is how it works and where its limits are.
paragraphs: Starting ink keys at a default and dialing them in by hand is one of the slowest parts of makeready. Every zone has to be read, judged and adjusted, and the press wastes sheets while the operator converges on target.

CIP3 and its successor CIP4 are workflow standards that move data between prepress, press and postpress. The relevant piece here is ink presetting: the Print Production Format (PPF), and later CIP4/JDF, carry ink-coverage information from prepress to the press console.

Presetting works from the plate. The RIP computes how much ink each key zone needs from the coverage of the separations, and the console opens the keys accordingly. The press starts close to target instead of flat.
The makeready gain is immediate: starting close means fewer pulls before the first good sheet, which is less paper, ink and time on every job.

Presetting and closed-loop are complementary. Presetting gets you close fast; closed-loop then drives the press into DeltaE tolerance and holds it through the run. Together they remove the most makeready waste.

There are practical conditions. The preset curves must be calibrated to the press and substrate, and the prepress data has to be clean. When that is in place, presetting is close to free savings on every job.
If you want to size the gain for your own production, the Rutherford ROI tool estimates the saved sheets and time, and a free console validation confirms what your press supports.

body.text: CIP3/CIP4 presetting is one of the cheapest ways to shorten makeready: it opens your ink keys from prepress data instead of from zero. Here is how it works, where it helps most, and where its limits are.
What CIP3/CIP4 presetting does

During ripping, the prepress system calculates how much ink each zone of the press will need, based on the image area in that zone. The press reads that file and sets its ink keys before the run starts, so the first sheets land far closer to target than a manual default would.
PPF versus JDF

CIP3 uses the older PPF format, carrying ink-key presetting data. CIP4 extends this with JDF, a richer job ticket that can also carry register, scheduling and production data. Both serve the same core purpose at the press: start close, not from zero.
Where it pairs with closed-loop

Presetting gets you to the doorstep; closed-loop walks you through it. Presetting opens the keys to roughly the right place, then closed-loop measures the printed sheet and fine-tunes each zone into tolerance, in fewer pulls than either method alone.
Limits to know

items: Presetting is open-loop: it does not see the printed result, so it cannot correct drift on its own.
Accuracy depends on clean prepress data and a well-characterized press.
Substrate, ink and press condition still move the target during the run.

de.title: CIP3/CIP4-Farbpresetting
de.excerpt: Was CIP3/CIP4-Farbpresetting (PPF, JDF) ist, wie es die Farbzonenschrauben aus Prepress-Daten öffnet und wie es mit Closed-Loop-Farbe das Einrichten verkürzt.
de.lead: CIP3/CIP4-Presetting ist einer der günstigsten Wege, das Einrichten zu verkürzen: Es öffnet Ihre Farbzonenschrauben aus den Prepress-Daten statt von null. So funktioniert es und das sind seine Grenzen.

body.text: CIP3/CIP4-Presetting ist einer der günstigsten Wege, das Einrichten zu verkürzen: Es öffnet Ihre Farbzonenschrauben aus den Prepress-Daten statt von null. Hier ist, wie es funktioniert, wo es am meisten hilft und wo seine Grenzen liegen.
Was CIP3/CIP4-Presetting leistet

Beim Rippen berechnet das Prepress-System, wie viel Farbe jede Zone der Druckmaschine benötigt, basierend auf der Bildfläche in dieser Zone. Die Druckmaschine liest diese Datei und stellt ihre Farbzonenschrauben vor dem Auflagenstart ein, sodass die ersten Bogen weit näher am Zielwert landen als bei einer manuellen Voreinstellung.
PPF gegenüber JDF

CIP3 nutzt das ältere PPF-Format, das die Presetting-Daten der Farbzonen trägt. CIP4 erweitert dies mit JDF, einem reichhaltigeren Job-Ticket, das auch Register-, Planungs- und Produktionsdaten transportieren kann. Beide erfüllen an der Druckmaschine denselben Kernzweck: nahe starten, nicht von null.
Wo es mit Closed-Loop zusammenspielt

Das Presetting bringt Sie bis vor die Tür; Closed-Loop führt Sie hindurch. Das Presetting öffnet die Schrauben ungefähr an die richtige Stelle, dann misst Closed-Loop den gedruckten Bogen und stimmt jede Zone in die Toleranz ab, in weniger Druckgängen als jede Methode für sich.
Grenzen, die man kennen sollte

items: Presetting ist Open-Loop: Es sieht das gedruckte Ergebnis nicht und kann eine Drift daher nicht selbst korrigieren.
Die Genauigkeit hängt von sauberen Prepress-Daten und einer gut charakterisierten Druckmaschine ab.
Bedruckstoff, Farbe und Maschinenzustand verschieben den Zielwert während der Auflage weiterhin.

fr.title: Presetting d'encrage CIP3/CIP4
fr.excerpt: Ce qu'est le presetting d'encrage CIP3/CIP4 (PPF, JDF), comment il ouvre les clés d'encrage à partir des données prépresse, et comment il s'associe au closed-loop pour raccourcir le calage.
fr.lead: Le presetting CIP3/CIP4 est l'un des moyens les moins chers de raccourcir le calage : il ouvre vos clés d'encrage à partir des données prépresse plutôt que de zéro. Voici comment il fonctionne et où sont ses limites.

body.text: Le presetting CIP3/CIP4 est l'un des moyens les moins chers de raccourcir le calage : il ouvre vos clés d'encrage à partir des données prépresse plutôt que de zéro. Voici comment il fonctionne, où il aide le plus, et où sont ses limites.
Ce que fait le presetting CIP3/CIP4

Lors du rip, le système prépresse calcule la quantité d'encre nécessaire à chaque zone de la presse, d'après la surface d'image dans cette zone. La presse lit ce fichier et règle ses clés d'encrage avant le démarrage, si bien que les premières feuilles tombent bien plus près de la cible qu'un réglage par défaut manuel.
PPF face à JDF

Le CIP3 utilise l'ancien format PPF, qui porte les données de presetting des clés d'encrage. Le CIP4 l'étend avec le JDF, un ticket de travail plus riche qui peut aussi transporter le repérage, la planification et des données de production. Les deux remplissent le même rôle de fond à la presse : démarrer proche, pas de zéro.
Où il s'associe au closed-loop

Le presetting vous amène jusqu'à la porte ; le closed-loop vous fait entrer. Le presetting ouvre les clés à peu près au bon endroit, puis le closed-loop mesure la feuille imprimée et affine chaque zone dans la tolérance, en moins de passes que chaque méthode seule.
Les limites à connaître

items: Le presetting est open-loop : il ne voit pas le résultat imprimé, il ne peut donc pas corriger une dérive de lui-même.
La précision dépend de données prépresse propres et d'une presse bien caractérisée.
Le substrat, l'encre et l'état de la presse déplacent encore la cible pendant le tirage.

it.lead: Il preset CIP3/CIP4 è uno dei modi più economici per accorciare l'avviamento: apre le chiavi di inchiostro dai dati di prestampa anziché da zero. Ecco come funziona e dove sono i suoi limiti.

body.text: Il preset CIP3/CIP4 è uno dei modi più economici per accorciare l'avviamento: apre le chiavi di inchiostro dai dati di prestampa anziché da zero. Ecco come funziona, dove aiuta di più e dove sono i suoi limiti.
Cosa fa il preset CIP3/CIP4

Durante il rip, il sistema di prestampa calcola quanto inchiostro servirà a ogni zona della macchina, in base all'area immagine in quella zona. La macchina legge quel file e imposta le chiavi di inchiostro prima dell'avvio, così i primi fogli cadono molto più vicini al target di un'impostazione predefinita manuale.
PPF rispetto a JDF

Il CIP3 usa il vecchio formato PPF, che porta i dati di preset delle chiavi di inchiostro. Il CIP4 lo estende con il JDF, un job ticket più ricco che può trasportare anche registro, pianificazione e dati di produzione. Entrambi servono lo stesso scopo di fondo in macchina: partire vicini, non da zero.
Dove si abbina al closed-loop

Il preset porta fino alla porta; il closed-loop fa entrare. Il preset apre le chiavi all'incirca al punto giusto, poi il closed-loop misura il foglio stampato e affina ogni zona in tolleranza, in meno passaggi di quanto faccia ciascun metodo da solo.
I limiti da conoscere

items: Il preset è open-loop: non vede il risultato stampato, quindi non può correggere da solo una deriva.
La precisione dipende da dati di prestampa puliti e da una macchina ben caratterizzata.
Supporto, inchiostro e condizioni della macchina spostano comunque il target durante la tiratura.

es.title: Preajuste de entintado CIP3/CIP4
es.excerpt: Qué es el preajuste de entintado CIP3/CIP4 (PPF, JDF), cómo abre las llaves de tinta desde los datos de preimpresión y cómo se combina con closed-loop para acortar la puesta a punto.
es.lead: El preajuste CIP3/CIP4 es una de las formas más baratas de acortar la puesta a punto: abre sus llaves de tinta desde los datos de preimpresión en lugar de desde cero. Así funciona y estos son sus límites.

body.text: El preajuste CIP3/CIP4 es una de las formas más baratas de acortar la puesta a punto: abre sus llaves de tinta desde los datos de preimpresión en lugar de desde cero. Así funciona, dónde ayuda más y dónde están sus límites.
Qué hace el preajuste CIP3/CIP4

Durante el rip, el sistema de preimpresión calcula cuánta tinta necesitará cada zona de la prensa, según el área de imagen en esa zona. La prensa lee ese archivo y ajusta sus llaves de tinta antes del arranque, de modo que los primeros pliegos caen mucho más cerca del objetivo que un valor por defecto manual.
PPF frente a JDF

El CIP3 usa el formato más antiguo PPF, que lleva los datos de preajuste de las llaves de tinta. El CIP4 lo amplía con JDF, un ticket de trabajo más rico que también puede transportar registro, planificación y datos de producción. Ambos cumplen el mismo propósito de fondo en la prensa: arrancar cerca, no desde cero.
Dónde se combina con closed-loop

El preajuste le lleva hasta la puerta; el closed-loop le hace entrar. El preajuste abre las llaves aproximadamente en el lugar correcto, luego el closed-loop mide el pliego impreso y afina cada zona en tolerancia, en menos pasadas que cualquiera de los dos métodos por separado.
Límites que conviene conocer

items: El preajuste es open-loop: no ve el resultado impreso, por lo que no puede corregir una deriva por sí solo.
La precisión depende de datos de preimpresión limpios y de una prensa bien caracterizada.
El sustrato, la tinta y el estado de la prensa siguen moviendo el objetivo durante la tirada.

title: Offset360
excerpt: The X-Rite + Rutherford closed-loop bundle for sheetfed offset. Discover the dedicated page.
lead: Offset360 is the X-Rite + Rutherford bundle that pairs IntelliTrax2 scanning, MeasureColor reporting and Rutherford ColorLoop closed-loop control into a single workflow for sheetfed offset printing. The dedicated landing page is at rutherford.fr/offset360.
paragraphs: Offset360 is not a new product. It is a bundle, a packaged way to deploy three best-of-breed pieces of color technology that have lived in different conversations for too long. IntelliTrax2 measures, MeasureColor reports, Rutherford ColorLoop closes the loop on the console. Together they form a single, opinionated workflow for sheetfed offset.

The bundle was built jointly by X-Rite and Rutherford for a specific reason: most printers already own the measurement device, sometimes the software, but they rarely have a working closed-loop on the press. The result is that color is measured, reports are generated, audits are filed, but the operator still chases the color manually at the start of every job. Offset360 was designed to fix that gap.

IntelliTrax2 is the desktop spectrophotometer that does the scanning. It reads a full color bar in under ten seconds, at 45°/0° geometry, supporting M0, M1 and M3 conditions in a single pass. Color bars can go down to 2 mm. It is the de-facto press-side scanner across the European packaging industry.

MeasureColor is the production color management platform, now part of X-Rite since the ColorWare acquisition in November 2024. It aggregates measurement data from the press, the proof and the brand standard, computes ΔE in real time, and produces audit-ready reports in PQX, CXF and CGATS formats. For a brand owner, MeasureColor is the layer that converts press data into something the supply chain can act on.

Rutherford ColorLoop is the closed-loop layer. It takes the deltas computed by MeasureColor, converts them into ink-key corrections, and pushes them directly to the press console. The operator validates and continues. The loop is closed, the color OK is reached faster, and the press stays in spec across the run. ColorLoop is also what makes the bundle press-agnostic, Heidelberg, Komori, Koenig & Bauer, Manroland, Mitsubishi, Ryobi all integrate.

On the press floor, the impact is measurable on three numbers: makeready waste comes down (typically around 50 percent on shops that adopt the loop discipline), setup time drops by roughly a third because key corrections happen automatically instead of by ear, and in-run color stability holds below ΔE 2 once the loop is running. The fourth, less visible number, is traceability, every sheet, every measurement, every correction is logged.

Offset360 is built for packaging converters who serve brand owners with strict color tolerances, for commercial offset shops running short-to-medium jobs where setup time dominates the cost structure, and for brand owners who want certainty that their color is reproducible across plants and suppliers. It works at its best where the entire chain, proof, plate, press, audit, is treated as one system rather than three.

The dedicated Offset360 landing page on rutherford.fr explains the bundle, the workflow, and the audiences in detail. It also links back to X-Rite's official Offset360 solution page for the product specs, datasheets and the X-Rite side of the support story. If you want to evaluate Offset360 on your own machine, the fastest entry point is the console validation form on rutherford.fr, send a few photos of your console and the press, and we come back with a scope tailored to the machines, the jobs and the brand standards on the floor.

title: PPWR & DPP
excerpt: A practical guide to PPWR and DPP readiness for packaging, labels, and offset printing operations serving the European market.
lead: What the new EU packaging rules and Digital Product Passport model mean for offset printers, converters, and print supply chains.
paragraphs: PPWR and Digital Product Passport requirements are becoming strategic topics for packaging printers and converters. Even when the detailed obligations vary by product category, the direction is clear: packaging and printed products sold into the European market will require stronger data, better traceability, and clearer evidence of compliance.

The Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) entered into force in February 2025 and will generally apply from August 2026. According to the European Commission, the regulation is designed to reduce packaging waste, improve recyclability, increase recycled content where relevant, and harmonize packaging rules across the EU market.

In parallel, the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation introduces the Digital Product Passport concept. The European Commission describes the DPP as a digital identity card for products, components, and materials, built to support sustainability, circularity, and legal compliance. GS1 also frames the DPP as a digital record that improves traceability and transparency throughout the value chain.

For offset printing companies, the operational implication is straightforward: product, substrate, job, and quality data will matter more. Printers that can connect production data, specifications, approvals, and traceability records in a structured way will be better positioned to answer customer requests and future compliance checks.

This does not mean every printer needs to rebuild its workflow overnight. It does mean that investments in standardization, connected quality systems, and better production visibility are becoming more strategic. The print businesses that prepare now will be in a stronger position to support brand owners, packaging buyers, and regulatory expectations over the next few years.

paragraphs: “Playing the piano” on a press console is a familiar image in offset printing: operators chasing color manually across the width of the sheet, one key at a time. It is also a sign that the preset and control workflow is not doing enough on its own.

The answer is not removing operator expertise. It is giving operators a better starting point through stronger presets, better measurement, and a more responsive closed-loop system.
The less the team has to “play the piano,” the faster it can reach target color, reduce waste, and make repeat jobs more predictable. That is the production logic behind the ColorLoop message.

lead: Why return on investment in offset print automation should be measured through waste reduction, time savings, and repeatability.
paragraphs: In offset printing, ROI is rarely driven by one spectacular metric. It is usually built through many small operational gains: fewer startup sheets, shorter makeready, less manual correction, and better repeatability on repeat jobs.

That is why Rutherford frames ROI through real production behavior. If a plant can reach color faster and hold quality more consistently, it saves substrate, operator time, and rework across the full year.
The financial effect is often stronger than expected because the same improvements touch multiple cost areas at once: paper, ink, labor, downtime, and customer-facing quality issues.
Viewed this way, automation is not only a technical upgrade. It is a decision about how efficiently the pressroom converts time and materials into sellable sheets.
